headline_marked: World Cup 2026: [[Germany-Paraguay match goes to extra time]] after 1-1 draw
headline: World Cup 2026: Germany-Paraguay match goes to extra time after 1-1 draw
summary: Paraguay took an early lead, but Kai Havertz equalized for Germany in the second half of the Round of 32 clash in Boston.
details: The Round of 32 clash between Germany and Paraguay in the 2026 World Cup has headed into extra time after the match ended 1-1 in regulation time.
Paraguay stunned Germany in the 42nd minute of the first half with a goal by Julio Enciso.
Germany fought back in the second half, with Arsenal forward Kai Havertz scoring a header in the 54th minute to level the score.
Analysts suggest that physical fatigue could play a role in extra time, as Paraguay started their tournament two days earlier than Germany.
This marks the fourth match for Paraguay in 18 days and the fourth for Germany in 16 days, with Germany having slightly less rest time overall.
The winner of this match will advance to the Round of 16 and face either France or Sweden in Philadelphia.
caption:
A World Cup thriller in Boston! Germany and Paraguay are locked in a 1-1 battle and head into extra time.

The Round of 32 clash between Germany and Paraguay in the 2026 World Cup has headed into extra time after the match ended 1-1 in regulation time.

Paraguay stunned Germany in the 42nd minute of the first half with a goal by Julio Enciso.

Germany fought back in the second half, with Arsenal forward Kai Havertz scoring a header in the 54th minute to level the score.

Analysts suggest that physical fatigue could play a role in extra time, as Paraguay started their tournament two days earlier than Germany.

This marks the fourth match for Paraguay in 18 days and the fourth for Germany in 16 days, with Germany having slightly less rest time overall.

The winner of this match will advance to the Round of 16 and face either France or Sweden in Philadelphia.

headline: Bangladesh trail by 230 runs as Zimbabwe build commanding lead in Harare Test
summary: Bangladesh are on the backfoot after losing an early wicket in their second innings, trailing Zimbabwe by 230 runs at the end of Day 2.
details: Bangladesh are struggling in their one-off Test against Zimbabwe at the Harare Sports Club, ending Day 2 at 40-1 in their second innings.
The team trails by 230 runs after Zimbabwe established a massive 270-run first innings lead.
Zimbabwe was bowled out for 410 in response to Bangladesh's first innings total of 140.
Opener Innocent Kaia starred for Zimbabwe, scoring 140 for his first Test century upon returning to the team after three years.
Other key contributions came from Wessly Madhevere (77), Craig Ervine (60), and Brian Bennett (59).
Despite the large total, Taijul Islam fought hard for Bangladesh, claiming 7 wickets for 138 runs.
In the second innings, Shadman Islam was dismissed near the close of play, caught at slip by Ben Curran off the bowling of Richard Ngarava.
Mahmudul Hasan Joy and Mominul Haque will resume the batting on Tuesday as Bangladesh fight to stay in the match.
caption:
Trailing by 230 runs and already losing a wicket in the second innings—Bangladesh is in deep trouble in Harare.

Bangladesh are struggling in their one-off Test against Zimbabwe at the Harare Sports Club, ending Day 2 at 40-1 in their second innings.

The team trails by 230 runs after Zimbabwe established a massive 270-run first innings lead.

Zimbabwe was bowled out for 410 in response to Bangladesh's first innings total of 140.

Opener Innocent Kaia starred for Zimbabwe, scoring 140 for his first Test century upon returning to the team after three years.

Other key contributions came from Wessly Madhevere (77), Craig Ervine (60), and Brian Bennett (59).

Despite the large total, Taijul Islam fought hard for Bangladesh, claiming 7 wickets for 138 runs.

In the second innings, Shadman Islam was dismissed near the close of play, caught at slip by Ben Curran off the bowling of Richard Ngarava.

Mahmudul Hasan Joy and Mominul Haque will resume the batting on Tuesday as Bangladesh fight to stay in the match.
